questions.reason: The sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational.
questions.answer: a
questions.explanation: Both are true and R explains A: 2√5 is irrational (a non-zero rational times an irrational), and adding the rational number 3 to it gives an irrational number.

questions.assertion: For any two positive integers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.
questions.reason: For any three positive integers p, q and r, HCF(p, q, r) × LCM(p, q, r) = p × q × r.
questions.answer: c
questions.explanation: A is true. R is false: for 6, 72 and 120, HCF = 6 and LCM = 360, so HCF × LCM = 2160, but 6 × 72 × 120 = 51840.

questions.stem: Express 5005 as a product of its prime factors.
valuePoints: Divides successively by primes: 5, then 7, then 11

questions.stem: Explain why 7 × 11 × 13 + 13 is a composite number.
questions.answer: 7 × 11 × 13 + 13 = 13 × (7 × 11 + 1) = 13 × 78 = 1014. It has factors other than 1 and itself (13 and 78), so it is composite.
valuePoints: Takes 13 out as a common factor: 13 × (77 + 1) = 13 × 78
Concludes it has a factor other than 1 and itself, so it is composite

rubric.label: Conclusion
rubric.descriptor: States it has factors other than 1 and itself, hence composite

questions.stem: Given that HCF(306, 657) = 9, find LCM(306, 657).
questions.answer: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers, so LCM = (306 × 657) ÷ 9 = 201042 ÷ 9 = 22338.

questions.stem: Find the HCF and LCM of 12, 15 and 21 by the prime factorisation method.
questions.answer: 12 = 2² × 3, 15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7. HCF = product of the smallest power of each common prime factor = 3. LCM = product of the greatest power of each prime factor involved = 2² × 3 × 5 × 7 = 420.

questions.stem: Given that √3 is irrational, prove that 5 − √3 is irrational.
questions.answer: Assume, to the contrary, that 5 − √3 is rational. Then 5 − √3 = a/b for some integers a, b with b ≠ 0. So √3 = 5 − a/b = (5b − a)/b. Since a and b are integers, (5b − a)/b is rational, so √3 would be rational. This contradicts the fact that √3 is irrational. Hence 5 − √3 is irrational.
valuePoints: Assumes 5 − √3 = a/b, a and b integers, b ≠ 0
Rearranges to √3 = (5b − a)/b, which is rational
Contradiction with √3 irrational, so 5 − √3 is irrational

rubric.label: Assumption
rubric.descriptor: Supposes 5 − √3 is rational and writes it as a/b, b ≠ 0

rubric.label: Contradiction and conclusion
rubric.descriptor: Names the contradiction and concludes 5 − √3 is irrational

questions.stem: Find the largest number which divides 245 and 1029, leaving a remainder of 5 in each case.
questions.answer: The number must divide 245 − 5 = 240 and 1029 − 5 = 1024 exactly. 240 = 2⁴ × 3 × 5 and 1024 = 2¹⁰. HCF(240, 1024) = 2⁴ = 16. The required number is 16 (and 16 > 5, so a remainder of 5 is possible).

rubric.label: Answer
rubric.descriptor: HCF = 16, stated as the required number

questions.stem: Prove that √5 is irrational. Hence show that 2√5 − 3 is irrational.
questions.answer: Suppose √5 is rational. Then √5 = a/b, where a and b are integers with no common factor other than 1 and b ≠ 0. So √5 b = a; squaring, 5b² = a². Hence 5 divides a², and since 5 is prime, 5 divides a. Write a = 5c. Then 5b² = 25c², so b² = 5c². Hence 5 divides b², so 5 divides b. Now 5 is a common factor of a and b, which contradicts that a and b have no common factor other than 1. So √5 is irrational. Next, suppose 2√5 − 3 = p/q, p and q integers, q ≠ 0. Then √5 = (p + 3q)/(2q), which is rational, contradicting what was just proved. Hence 2√5 − 3 is irrational.
valuePoints: Assumes √5 = a/b in lowest terms and gets 5b² = a²
5 divides a² so 5 divides a; writes a = 5c
Gets b² = 5c², so 5 divides b — contradiction with coprimality

rubric.label: Assumption in lowest terms
rubric.descriptor: √5 = a/b, a and b coprime, b ≠ 0, leading to 5b² = a²

rubric.label: 5 divides a
rubric.descriptor: Uses the prime-divides-square result; writes a = 5c

rubric.label: 5 divides b and contradiction
rubric.descriptor: b² = 5c², so 5 divides b; contradiction stated

rubric.label: Final conclusion
rubric.descriptor: Rational √5 contradicts the first part, so 2√5 − 3 is irrational

questions.stem: (i) Three school bells ring at intervals of 12 minutes, 18 minutes and 30 minutes. If they ring together at 8:00 a.m., when will they next ring together? (ii) Two water tanks hold 850 litres and 680 litres. Find the capacity of the largest container that can measure the water of either tank an exact number of times.
questions.answer: (i) 12 = 2² × 3, 18 = 2 × 3², 30 = 2 × 3 × 5. LCM = 2² × 3² × 5 = 180 minutes = 3 hours. They ring together again at 11:00 a.m. (ii) 850 = 2 × 5² × 17, 680 = 2³ × 5 × 17. HCF = 2 × 5 × 17 = 170. The largest container holds 170 litres (850 = 5 × 170 and 680 = 4 × 170).
valuePoints: Recognises (i) as an LCM problem and (ii) as an HCF problem

questions.passage: For the annual sports day, a school has 96 boys and 120 girls in the march past. The sports teacher wants to arrange them in rows so that every row has the same number of students and each row has only boys or only girls. She also wants the number of rows to be as small as possible, so she must put as many students as she can in each row.

parts.prompt: The prime factorisation of 96 is:
parts.answer: (b) — 96 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2⁵ × 3. Option (c) contains 4, which is not prime.

parts.prompt: What is the greatest number of students she can put in each row?
How many rows will there be in all? Show your working.
parts.answer: Rows of boys = 96 ÷ 24 = 4; rows of girls = 120 ÷ 24 = 5; total = 9 rows. (1 mark: both divisions by 24; 1 mark: 9 rows.)

questions.assertion: The graph of y = x² − 4 meets the x-axis at exactly two points.
questions.reason: A quadratic polynomial can have at most two zeroes.
questions.answer: b
questions.explanation: Both are true. A holds because x² − 4 has two zeroes, 2 and −2. R only says there are at most two; it does not explain why this graph meets the axis at exactly two points.

questions.reason: A polynomial of degree 2 is called a quadratic polynomial.
questions.answer: d
questions.explanation: A is false: the term 2√x has exponent ½, which is not a whole number, so the expression is not a polynomial at all. R is true.

questions.stem: Find the sum and the product of the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial 3x² − 5x + 2.
questions.answer: Here a = 3, b = −5, c = 2. Sum of zeroes = −b/a = 5/3. Product of zeroes = c/a = 2/3.

questions.stem: Find a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes have sum −3 and product 2.
questions.answer: A quadratic polynomial with sum of zeroes S and product P is k(x² − Sx + P). So the polynomial is x² − (−3)x + 2 = x² + 3x + 2 (or any non-zero multiple of it).

rubric.label: Form
rubric.descriptor: Writes x² − (sum of zeroes)x + (product of zeroes)

questions.stem: If 2 is a zero of the polynomial x² + kx − 10, find the value of k and the other zero.
questions.answer: p(2) = 4 + 2k − 10 = 0, so k = 3. The polynomial is x² + 3x − 10 = (x + 5)(x − 2), so the other zero is −5. (Check: product of zeroes = 2 × (−5) = −10 = c/a.)

rubric.label: Other zero
rubric.descriptor: −5, by factorising or using the product of zeroes

questions.stem: Find the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial 6x² − 3 − 7x and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.

rubric.label: Verification
rubric.descriptor: Sum and product both checked against −b/a and c/a; ½ mark each

questions.stem: If α and β are the zeroes of the polynomial 2x² − 4x + 1, find, without finding the zeroes, the values of (i) α² + β² (ii) 1/α + 1/β.

The graph of y = p(x), where p(x) is a quadratic polynomial with leading coefficient 1, is a parabola opening upwards that cuts the x-axis at the points (−2, 0) and (3, 0) and the y-axis at (0, −6). (i) How many zeroes does p(x) have? (ii) What are they? (iii) Write p(x).
questions.answer: (i) The graph meets the x-axis at two points, so p(x) has 2 zeroes. (ii) The zeroes are the x-coordinates of these points: −2 and 3. (iii) p(x) = (x + 2)(x − 3) = x² − x − 6. Check: p(0) = −6, which matches the point (0, −6).
valuePoints: Two zeroes, because the graph cuts the x-axis twice

questions.stem: Find the zeroes of each of the following quadratic polynomials and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients: (i) 4u² + 8u (ii) t² − 15.
questions.answer: (i) 4u² + 8u = 4u(u + 2), so the zeroes are 0 and −2. Sum = −2 = −8/4 = −b/a; product = 0 = 0/4 = c/a. (ii) t² − 15 = (t − √15)(t + √15), so the zeroes are √15 and −√15. Sum = 0 = −0/1 = −b/a; product = −15 = −15/1 = c/a.
valuePoints: Verifies sum −2 = −b/a and product 0 = c/a for (i)
Verifies sum 0 = −b/a and product −15 = c/a for (ii)

rubric.label: Verification of (i)
rubric.descriptor: Sum and product checked; ½ for each with the coefficients identified

rubric.label: Verification of (ii)
rubric.descriptor: Sum and product checked, noting b = 0

questions.stem: If α and β are the zeroes of the polynomial x² − 3x − 4, find a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes are 2α + 1 and 2β + 1. Verify your answer by finding α and β.
questions.answer: α + β = 3, αβ = −4. New sum = (2α + 1) + (2β + 1) = 2(α + β) + 2 = 8. New product = (2α + 1)(2β + 1) = 4αβ + 2(α + β) + 1 = −16 + 6 + 1 = −9. Required polynomial: x² − 8x − 9 (or any non-zero multiple). Verification: x² − 3x − 4 = (x − 4)(x + 1), so α, β = 4 and −1; new zeroes are 9 and −1, and x² − 8x − 9 = (x − 9)(x + 1). ✓

rubric.label: Sum and product of α, β
Verification
rubric.descriptor: Finds α, β = 4, −1 and confirms zeroes 9 and −1

questions.passage: In a school garden, a sprinkler throws a jet of water that falls back to the ground. Taking the ground as the x-axis, the path of the jet is the graph of p(x) = −x² + 8x − 12, where x is the horizontal distance in metres from a marker post. The jet leaves the ground at one point and lands at another, and both points lie on the x-axis. The gardener wants to know where to place plants so that they get water.

parts.prompt: How many zeroes does p(x) have, as shown by the path of the jet?
parts.answer: (c) — the path meets the x-axis at two points, so p(x) has two zeroes.

parts.prompt: Find the zeroes of p(x).
parts.answer: −x² + 8x − 12 = −(x² − 8x + 12) = −(x − 2)(x − 6), so the zeroes are 2 and 6 (the jet leaves at 2 m and lands at 6 m from the post).

parts.prompt: Verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients of p(x).

questions.assertion: The pair of equations x + 2y = 4 and 2x + 4y = 12 is inconsistent.
questions.reason: If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, the lines representing the equations are parallel and have no common point.
questions.answer: a
questions.explanation: Here a₁/a₂ = 1/2, b₁/b₂ = 2/4 = 1/2 and c₁/c₂ = 4/12 = 1/3. So a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂: the lines are parallel, there is no solution, and the pair is inconsistent. Both are true and R explains A.

questions.assertion: The pair of equations 3x − y = 7 and 6x − 2y = 14 has a unique solution.
questions.reason: For this pair, a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂, so the lines coincide.
questions.answer: d
questions.explanation: 3/6 = −1/−2 = 7/14 = 1/2, so the lines coincide and there are infinitely many solutions. A is false; R is true.

questions.stem: Without solving, find out whether the pair of equations 5x − 4y + 8 = 0 and 7x + 6y − 9 = 0 is consistent or inconsistent.
questions.answer: a₁/a₂ = 5/7 and b₁/b₂ = −4/6 = −2/3. Since 5/7 ≠ −2/3, the lines intersect at one point: the pair has a unique solution and is consistent.
valuePoints: Unequal, so a unique solution: consistent

questions.stem: Solve by the substitution method: x + y = 14 and x − y = 4.
questions.answer: From the second equation, x = y + 4. Substituting in the first: y + 4 + y = 14, so 2y = 10 and y = 5. Then x = 5 + 4 = 9. Solution: x = 9, y = 5.

rubric.label: Substitution
rubric.descriptor: One variable expressed and substituted, giving y = 5 (or x = 9)

questions.stem: Find the value of k for which the pair of equations kx + 3y = k − 3 and 12x + ky = k has no solution.
questions.answer: For no solution, a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂. k/12 = 3/k gives k² = 36, so k = 6 or k = −6. For k = 6: c₁/c₂ = 3/6 = 1/2 = a₁/a₂, which gives infinitely many solutions, so reject. For k = −6: a₁/a₂ = −1/2 and c₁/c₂ = (−9)/(−6) = 3/2 ≠ −1/2. So k = −6.

questions.stem: Solve by the elimination method: 3x + 4y = 10 and 2x − 2y = 2.
questions.answer: Multiply the second equation by 2: 4x − 4y = 4. Add to the first: 7x = 14, so x = 2. Substitute in 2x − 2y = 2: 4 − 2y = 2, so y = 1. Check: 3(2) + 4(1) = 10 ✓.
valuePoints: Makes the coefficients of y equal and opposite: 4x − 4y = 4

questions.stem: For what values of a and b does the pair of equations 2x + 3y = 7 and (a − b)x + (a + b)y = 3a + b − 2 have infinitely many solutions?
questions.answer: For infinitely many solutions, 2/(a − b) = 3/(a + b) = 7/(3a + b − 2). From 2/(a − b) = 7/(3a + b − 2): 6a + 2b − 4 = 7a − 7b, so a − 9b = −4. From 2/(a − b) = 3/(a + b): 2a + 2b = 3a − 3b, so a = 5b. Then 5b − 9b = −4, b = 1 and a = 5. Check: 2/4 = 3/6 = 7/14.
valuePoints: Writes the condition a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂

rubric.label: Linear equations in a and b

questions.stem: Five years hence, the age of a father will be three times the age of his son. Five years ago, the father was seven times as old as his son. Find their present ages.
questions.answer: Let the father's present age be x years and the son's y years. x + 5 = 3(y + 5) gives x − 3y = 10. x − 5 = 7(y − 5) gives x − 7y = −30. Subtracting: 4y = 40, so y = 10 and x = 40. Father 40 years, son 10 years. Check: 45 = 3 × 15 and 35 = 7 × 5.

questions.stem: A fraction becomes 2/3 if 1 is added to both its numerator and denominator. If 5 is subtracted from both its numerator and denominator, it becomes 1/2. Find the fraction.
questions.answer: Let the fraction be x/y. (x + 1)/(y + 1) = 2/3 gives 3x + 3 = 2y + 2, i.e. 3x − 2y = −1. (x − 5)/(y − 5) = 1/2 gives 2x − 10 = y − 5, i.e. 2x − y = 5. From the second, y = 2x − 5. Substituting: 3x − 2(2x − 5) = −1, so −x + 10 = −1 and x = 11. Then y = 17. The fraction is 11/17. Check: 12/18 = 2/3 and 6/12 = 1/2.

rubric.label: Solving
rubric.descriptor: Substitution or elimination carried out correctly to x = 11, y = 17

rubric.label: Answer
rubric.descriptor: 11/17, with a check against both conditions

questions.stem: Draw the graphs of the equations x − y + 1 = 0 and 3x + 2y − 12 = 0 on the same axes. Determine the coordinates of the vertices of the triangle formed by these lines and the x-axis.
questions.answer: For x − y + 1 = 0 (y = x + 1): points (−1, 0), (0, 1), (2, 3). For 3x + 2y − 12 = 0 (y = (12 − 3x)/2): points (4, 0), (0, 6), (2, 3). The lines meet at (2, 3), since 2 − 3 + 1 = 0 and 6 + 6 − 12 = 0. The first line meets the x-axis at (−1, 0) and the second at (4, 0). Vertices of the triangle: (−1, 0), (4, 0) and (2, 3).
valuePoints: A table of at least two points for each line
Both lines drawn correctly on the same axes

rubric.label: Table for first line
rubric.descriptor: At least two correct points, e.g. (−1, 0), (2, 3)

rubric.label: Table for second line
rubric.descriptor: At least two correct points, e.g. (4, 0), (2, 3)

rubric.label: Graph
rubric.descriptor: Both lines plotted correctly on the same axes

questions.passage: A school holds a two-day science fair and sells entry tickets at a fixed price for adults and a lower fixed price for children. On the first day, a family bought 3 adult tickets and 5 child tickets for ₹390. On the second day, another family bought 2 adult tickets and 4 child tickets for ₹280. Let the price of an adult ticket be ₹x and that of a child ticket be ₹y.

parts.prompt: Which pair of equations describes the situation?
parts.answer: (a) — 3 adults at ₹x and 5 children at ₹y cost ₹390; 2 adults and 4 children cost ₹280.

parts.prompt: Without solving, state whether this pair has a unique solution, and why.
parts.answer: a₁/a₂ = 3/2 and b₁/b₂ = 5/4; since 3/2 ≠ 5/4 the lines intersect, so there is a unique solution.

parts.prompt: Find the price of each ticket.
parts.answer: Multiply the first equation by 2 and the second by 3: 6x + 10y = 780 and 6x + 12y = 840. Subtracting, 2y = 60, so y = 30; then 3x = 390 − 150 = 240, x = 80. Adult ticket ₹80, child ticket ₹30. (1 mark: elimination to y = 30; 1 mark: x = 80.)

questions.assertion: The quadratic equation 2x² − 4x + 3 = 0 has no real roots.
questions.reason: A quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 has no real roots if b² − 4ac < 0.
questions.answer: a
questions.explanation: b² − 4ac = 16 − 24 = −8 < 0, so there are no real roots. Both are true and R explains A.

questions.reason: An equation that contains a term in x³ can never be a quadratic equation.
questions.answer: c
questions.explanation: Expanding, x³ + 6x² + 12x + 8 = x³ − 4, which reduces to 6x² + 12x + 12 = 0, a quadratic equation; so A is true. R is false: this very equation contains x³ terms that cancel.

questions.stem: Find the roots of the quadratic equation x² − 3x − 10 = 0 by factorisation.

rubric.label: Roots
rubric.descriptor: 5 and −2; ½ mark for one root

questions.stem: Find the value of k for which the quadratic equation kx(x − 2) + 6 = 0 has two equal roots.
questions.answer: kx² − 2kx + 6 = 0, so a = k, b = −2k, c = 6. Equal roots need b² − 4ac = 0: 4k² − 24k = 0, 4k(k − 6) = 0. k = 0 is rejected (the equation would not be quadratic), so k = 6.

questions.stem: If one root of the quadratic equation 2x² + kx − 6 = 0 is 2, find the value of k and the other root.
questions.answer: Substituting x = 2: 8 + 2k − 6 = 0, so k = −1. Product of roots = c/a = −6/2 = −3, so the other root = −3 ÷ 2 = −3/2. (Check: 2x² − x − 6 = (2x + 3)(x − 2).)
valuePoints: Other root −3/2 using the product of roots (or factorising)

questions.stem: Find the roots of 2x² − 7x + 3 = 0 using the quadratic formula.
Find the nature of the roots of 3x² − 4√3x + 4 = 0. If the roots are real, find them.
questions.answer: a = 3, b = −4√3, c = 4. b² − 4ac = 48 − 48 = 0, so the roots are real and equal. Each root = −b/2a = 4√3/6 = 2√3/3 (= 2/√3). The roots are 2/√3, 2/√3.

questions.stem: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 306. Form a quadratic equation and find the integers.
questions.answer: Let the integers be x and x + 1. x(x + 1) = 306, so x² + x − 306 = 0. x² + 18x − 17x − 306 = (x + 18)(x − 17) = 0, so x = 17 or x = −18. The integers are positive, so x = 17: the integers are 17 and 18 (17 × 18 = 306).

rubric.label: Answer in context
rubric.descriptor: 17 and 18, with the negative root rejected

questions.stem: A train travels 360 km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 5 km/h more, it would have taken 1 hour less for the same journey. Find the speed of the train.
questions.answer: Let the speed be x km/h. Time taken = 360/x hours; at the higher speed, 360/(x + 5) hours. 360/x − 360/(x + 5) = 1, so 360(x + 5) − 360x = x(x + 5), i.e. 1800 = x² + 5x, or x² + 5x − 1800 = 0. (x + 45)(x − 40) = 0, so x = 40 or x = −45. Speed cannot be negative, so the speed is 40 km/h. Check: 360/40 = 9 h and 360/45 = 8 h.

questions.stem: The diagonal of a rectangular field is 60 m more than its shorter side. The longer side is 30 m more than the shorter side. Form a quadratic equation, solve it using the quadratic formula, and find the sides of the field.
questions.answer: Let the shorter side be x m. Longer side = x + 30, diagonal = x + 60. By Pythagoras, x² + (x + 30)² = (x + 60)². So 2x² + 60x + 900 = x² + 120x + 3600, giving x² − 60x − 2700 = 0. Here b² − 4ac = 3600 + 10800 = 14400, √14400 = 120. x = (60 ± 120)/2 = 90 or −30. Length cannot be negative, so x = 90. The sides are 90 m and 120 m (diagonal 150 m; 90² + 120² = 150²).
valuePoints: Sides x, x + 30 and diagonal x + 60

rubric.label: Setting up
rubric.descriptor: Pythagoras applied to x, x + 30, x + 60

rubric.label: Sides
rubric.descriptor: 90 m and 120 m, negative root rejected

questions.passage: The eco-club of a school is laying out a rectangular vegetable plot behind the library. The plot must have an area of 300 square metres, and because of the shape of the space available, its length has to be 5 metres more than its breadth. The club secretary lets the breadth of the plot be x metres and sets up an equation to find the dimensions before buying fencing.

parts.prompt: Which quadratic equation describes the plot?
parts.answer: (d) — breadth x, length x + 5, so x(x + 5) = 300, i.e. x² + 5x − 300 = 0.

parts.prompt: Find the discriminant of this equation and state the nature of its roots.
parts.answer: b² − 4ac = 25 + 1200 = 1225 > 0, so the roots are real and distinct.

parts.prompt: Find the length and breadth of the plot.
parts.answer: x = (−5 ± √1225)/2 = (−5 ± 35)/2 = 15 or −20. Breadth cannot be negative, so breadth = 15 m and length = 20 m (15 × 20 = 300). (1 mark: roots 15 and −20; 1 mark: dimensions with −20 rejected.)

questions.assertion: The list of numbers 2, 4, 8, 16, … is an arithmetic progression.
questions.reason: In an arithmetic progression, the difference between any two consecutive terms is the same.
questions.answer: d
questions.explanation: The differences are 2, 4, 8, …, which are not equal, so the list is not an AP: A is false. R is the true definition of an AP.

questions.assertion: The 10th term of the AP 5, 8, 11, … is 32.
questions.reason: The nth term of an AP with first term a and common difference d is aₙ = a + (n − 1)d.
questions.answer: a
questions.explanation: a₁₀ = 5 + 9 × 3 = 32, found using the formula in R. Both are true and R explains A.

questions.stem: Which term of the AP 3, 8, 13, 18, … is 78?
For what value of k are 2k + 1, 13 and 5k − 3 three consecutive terms of an AP?
questions.answer: For consecutive terms of an AP, 2 × 13 = (2k + 1) + (5k − 3). So 26 = 7k − 2, 7k = 28 and k = 4. The terms are 9, 13, 17, with common difference 4.

questions.stem: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of the AP 1, 4, 7, 10, ….
valuePoints: Uses Sₙ = n/2[2a + (n − 1)d] with a = 1, d = 3

questions.stem: The 3rd term of an AP is 16 and its 7th term exceeds its 5th term by 12. Find the AP.
How many terms of the AP 9, 17, 25, … must be taken to give a sum of 636?
Find the 10th term from the last term of the AP 4, 9, 14, …, 254.
questions.answer: Read from the end, the AP is 254, 249, 244, …, with first term 254 and common difference −5. The 10th term from the end = 254 + 9 × (−5) = 254 − 45 = 209. (Alternatively: the AP has (254 − 4)/5 + 1 = 51 terms, and the 10th from the end is the 42nd term = 4 + 41 × 5 = 209.)
valuePoints: Reverses the AP: first term 254, d = −5

rubric.label: Reversed AP
rubric.descriptor: a = 254, d = −5 (or identifies it as the 42nd term)

questions.stem: The sum of the first n terms of an AP is given by Sₙ = 4n − n². Find (i) the first term (ii) the sum of the first two terms (iii) the second term (iv) the 10th term (v) the nth term.

Ramya saves ₹50 in the first week of the year and then increases her weekly saving by ₹20 every week. (i) How much does she save in the 20th week? (ii) In which week does she save ₹330? (iii) How much does she save in total in the first 20 weeks?
valuePoints: Recognises an AP with a = 50, d = 20

questions.passage: A school auditorium is being fitted with seats for the annual day. The front row has 20 seats, and every row behind it has 2 seats more than the row in front of it. There are 25 rows in all. The principal wants to know how the seats are spread across the rows and how many guests the auditorium can hold.

parts.prompt: How many seats are there in the 10th row?
Which row has 50 seats?
parts.answer: 20 + (n − 1) × 2 = 50 gives n − 1 = 15, so the 16th row.

parts.prompt: How many seats are there in the auditorium altogether?
parts.answer: Last row a₂₅ = 20 + 24 × 2 = 68. S₂₅ = 25/2 (20 + 68) = 25 × 44 = 1100 seats. (1 mark: last row or formula; 1 mark: 1100.)

questions.assertion: Two quadrilaterals whose corresponding sides are proportional are always similar.
questions.reason: A square and a rhombus with equal sides have proportional sides but need not have equal corresponding angles.
questions.answer: d
questions.explanation: For polygons, proportional sides alone are not enough; the corresponding angles must also be equal. The square and rhombus in R are a counter-example, so A is false and R is true.

questions.assertion: A triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm is similar to a triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm.
questions.reason: If two angles of one triangle are respectively equal to two angles of another triangle, the two triangles are similar.
questions.answer: b
questions.explanation: A is true by the SSS criterion: 3/6 = 4/8 = 5/10 = 1/2. R (the AA criterion) is also true, but A follows from proportional sides, not from equal angles, so R does not explain A.

questions.stem: In △ABC, D is a point on AB and E is a point on AC such that DE ∥ BC. If AD = 1.5 cm, DB = 3 cm and AE = 1 cm, find EC.
questions.answer: By the Basic Proportionality Theorem, AD/DB = AE/EC. So 1.5/3 = 1/EC, giving EC = 3/1.5 = 2 cm.

questions.stem: E and F are points on the sides PQ and PR respectively of △PQR, with PE = 3.9 cm, EQ = 3 cm, PF = 3.6 cm and FR = 2.4 cm. State whether EF ∥ QR, giving a reason.
questions.answer: PE/EQ = 3.9/3 = 1.3 and PF/FR = 3.6/2.4 = 1.5. Since PE/EQ ≠ PF/FR, EF does not divide PQ and PR in the same ratio, so EF is not parallel to QR (by the Basic Proportionality Theorem).
valuePoints: Ratios unequal, so EF is not parallel to QR

questions.stem: In △ABC, ∠A = 50° and ∠B = 60°. In △PQR, ∠P = 50° and ∠R = 70°. Are the two triangles similar? If so, write the similarity with the correct correspondence and name the criterion.
questions.answer: ∠C = 180° − 50° − 60° = 70° and ∠Q = 180° − 50° − 70° = 60°. So ∠A = ∠P, ∠B = ∠Q and ∠C = ∠R. Hence △ABC ~ △PQR by the AA (or AAA) similarity criterion.

questions.stem: In △ABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. If AD = x cm, DB = (x − 2) cm, AE = (x + 2) cm and EC = (x − 1) cm, find the value of x.
questions.answer: By BPT, AD/DB = AE/EC: x/(x − 2) = (x + 2)/(x − 1). Cross-multiplying, x(x − 1) = (x + 2)(x − 2), so x² − x = x² − 4 and x = 4. Check: AD = 4, DB = 2, AE = 6, EC = 3, and 4/2 = 6/3.

questions.stem: A vertical pole 2.4 m tall casts a shadow 1.6 m long on level ground. At the same time, a tree standing vertically on the same ground casts a shadow 12 m long. Using similar triangles, find the height of the tree.
questions.answer: The pole with its shadow and the tree with its shadow form two right triangles. Each has a right angle at the foot of the object, and the sun's rays make the same angle with the ground at the same time, so the triangles are similar by AA. Hence height of tree / 12 = 2.4/1.6, so height = 12 × 1.5 = 18 m.
valuePoints: Two right triangles, equal angles of elevation of the sun

rubric.label: Similarity
rubric.descriptor: Triangles similar by AA with reasons

questions.stem: △ABC ~ △DEF with AB = 4 cm, BC = 6 cm and CA = 5 cm. If DE = 6 cm, find EF, FD and the perimeter of △DEF.
questions.answer: In similar triangles corresponding sides are in the same ratio: DE/AB = EF/BC = FD/CA = 6/4 = 3/2. EF = 6 × 3/2 = 9 cm, FD = 5 × 3/2 = 7.5 cm. Perimeter of △DEF = 6 + 9 + 7.5 = 22.5 cm.

rubric.label: Sides
rubric.descriptor: EF = 9 cm and FD = 7.5 cm; ½ each

questions.stem: Prove that if a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio. (Take △ABC with a line parallel to BC meeting AB at D and AC at E; prove AD/DB = AE/EC. Describe any construction you use in words.)
questions.answer: Given: △ABC, DE ∥ BC, D on AB, E on AC. To prove: AD/DB = AE/EC. Construction: join BE and CD; draw DM ⊥ AC and EN ⊥ AB. Proof: ar(ADE) = ½ × AD × EN and ar(BDE) = ½ × DB × EN, so ar(ADE)/ar(BDE) = AD/DB. Similarly ar(ADE) = ½ × AE × DM and ar(DEC) = ½ × EC × DM, so ar(ADE)/ar(DEC) = AE/EC. △BDE and △DEC are on the same base DE and between the same parallels DE and BC, so ar(BDE) = ar(DEC). Hence AD/DB = AE/EC.
valuePoints: Given, to prove and construction stated
ar(BDE) = ar(DEC): same base DE, between the same parallels

rubric.label: Given, to prove, construction
rubric.descriptor: Join BE, CD; perpendiculars DM ⊥ AC and EN ⊥ AB

questions.stem: ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC. Its diagonals AC and BD intersect at O. (i) Prove that △AOB ~ △COD. (ii) Hence show that OA/OC = OB/OD. (iii) If AB = 2 CD and OA = 6 cm, find OC and AC.
questions.answer: (i) In △AOB and △COD: ∠AOB = ∠COD (vertically opposite angles); ∠OAB = ∠OCD (alternate angles, since AB ∥ DC and AC is a transversal). So △AOB ~ △COD by AA. (ii) Corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional: OA/OC = OB/OD = AB/CD. (iii) OA/OC = AB/CD = 2, so OC = 6/2 = 3 cm and AC = OA + OC = 9 cm.
valuePoints: Alternate angles equal because AB ∥ DC

questions.passage: A carpenter is building the triangular wooden frame ABC of a shed roof. The sloping beam AB is 6 m long, the other sloping beam AC is 7.5 m long, and the base beam BC is 9 m long. To strengthen the frame, she fixes a straight support DE parallel to BC, with D on AB and E on AC, so that AD = 2 m. She needs the lengths of the pieces before cutting the wood.

parts.prompt: What is the length AE?
parts.answer: (a) — since DE ∥ BC, AD/AB = AE/AC, so AE = 7.5 × 2/6 = 2.5 m.

parts.prompt: Name the criterion by which △ADE ~ △ABC, and give the reason.
parts.answer: AA: ∠A is common, and ∠ADE = ∠ABC (corresponding angles, DE ∥ BC).

parts.prompt: Find the length of the support DE and of the part EC of the beam.
parts.answer: DE/BC = AD/AB = 2/6, so DE = 9 × 1/3 = 3 m (1 mark). EC = AC − AE = 7.5 − 2.5 = 5 m (1 mark).

questions.assertion: The distance of the point (3, −4) from the x-axis is 4 units.
questions.reason: The distance of a point (x, y) from the x-axis is |x|.
questions.answer: c
questions.explanation: The distance of (x, y) from the x-axis is |y|, here |−4| = 4, so A is true. R is false: |x| is the distance from the y-axis.

questions.assertion: The mid-point of the line segment joining (2, 3) and (4, 7) is (3, 5).
questions.reason: The distance between the points (2, 3) and (4, 7) is 2√5 units.
questions.answer: b
questions.explanation: A: ((2 + 4)/2, (3 + 7)/2) = (3, 5), true. R: √(2² + 4²) = √20 = 2√5, true. The distance does not explain the mid-point, so the answer is (b).

questions.stem: The point (1, 2) is the mid-point of the line segment joining A(a, 4) and B(3, b). Find a and b.
Find the coordinates of the point which divides the line segment joining (−1, 7) and (4, −3) internally in the ratio 2 : 3.
In what ratio does the point (−4, 6) divide the line segment joining A(−6, 10) and B(3, −8)?
questions.answer: Let the ratio be k : 1. x-coordinate: (3k − 6)/(k + 1) = −4, so 3k − 6 = −4k − 4, 7k = 2 and k = 2/7. The ratio is 2 : 7. Check with y: (−8 × 2 + 10 × 7)/(2 + 7) = 54/9 = 6 ✓.
valuePoints: Takes the ratio k : 1 and uses the x-coordinate

questions.stem: Using the distance formula, show that the points A(1, 5), B(2, 3) and C(−2, 11) are collinear.
Show that the points A(1, −2), B(4, −1), C(3, 2) and D(0, 1), taken in order, are the vertices of a square.
questions.answer: AB = √[(4 − 1)² + (−1 + 2)²] = √10. BC = √[(3 − 4)² + (2 + 1)²] = √10. CD = √[(0 − 3)² + (1 − 2)²] = √10. DA = √[(1 − 0)² + (−2 − 1)²] = √10. Diagonal AC = √[(3 − 1)² + (2 + 2)²] = √20. Diagonal BD = √[(0 − 4)² + (1 + 1)²] = √20. All four sides are equal and the diagonals are equal, so ABCD is a square.
valuePoints: Equal sides and equal diagonals, so a square
